title: The unbearable hardness of deciding about magic
summary: Identifying the boundary between classical and quantum computation is a central challenge in quantum information. In multi-qubit systems, entanglement and magic are the key resources underlying genuinely quantum behaviour. While entanglement is well understood, magic - essential for universal quantum computation - remains relatively poorly characterised. Here we show that determining membership in the stabilizer polytope, which defines the free states of magic-state resource theory, requires super-exponential time $\class{exp} ( n^2)$ in the number of qubits $n$, even approximately.
